statement: The first line holds n. You climb a staircase of n stairs taking 1 or 2 steps at a time; print the number of distinct ways to reach the top. Split by the last move: every way ends with a single step from stair n-1 or a double from n-2, so the counts add - f(n) = f(n-1) + f(n-2) with f(0) = f(1) = 1. Roll two variables forward; the answer fits in a 64-bit integer for every allowed n.
constraints: The answer fits in a 64-bit integer.

example.why: 1+1+1+1, 1+1+2, 1+2+1, 2+1+1 and 2+2 - five ways, the fibonacci count.

hint: Two rolling variables are the whole table - only the last two counts are ever read.
mistake: Recursing without a memo; the twin branches turn n = 45 into billions of calls.
